name: @fuzdev/tsv-benches
description: tsv benchmark harness deps — the single source of truth for the npm package versions the bench measures against. Consumed by BOTH runtimes: Deno reads it via `nodeModulesDir: "manual"` in deno.json, Node reads it directly. Install with `npm install` (the one installer). The jsr-only `@std/*` packages, if any, stay in deno.json.
//canonical-sync: ⚠ The 5 canonical packages (prettier, svelte, acorn, @sveltejs/acorn-typescript, prettier-plugin-svelte) are ALSO pinned as literals in crates/tsv_debug/src/deno/sidecar.ts and resolved by the sidecar lockfile crates/tsv_debug/src/deno/deno.lock, and all three MUST match — agreement (and ../svelte / ../acorn-typescript checkout alignment, when present) is enforced by `deno task pins:audit` (scripts/check_canonical_pins.ts, in `deno task check`). Bumping any re-baselines the whole fixture corpus — see docs/benchmarks.md §'Canonical baseline is coupled'. The other deps (oxc, oxfmt, biome, etc.) are free to bump independently. ⚠ This lockfile's TRANSITIVE versions are NOT part of that contract and are deliberately not synced: `esrap` here sits at whatever npm resolved for svelte's caret range, which can differ from the sidecar lock's pin. That is fine — nothing in this harness ever calls svelte's `compile()` (lib/canonical.ts uses `parse`/`parseCss` only, and the reject cache is a PARSE harvest), so esrap is loaded but never invoked and cannot move a measured number. The sidecar lock is the authoritative pin because it is the one that decides oracle OUTPUT; aligning this file to it would mean an `overrides` entry plus an `npm install` that prunes the oxc wasi binding and can churn the measured toolchain, i.e. all risk and no effect.
//engines: Node ≥ 22.18 is the native TS type-stripping floor — the harness entries (bench.ts, install_deps.ts) run as TypeScript directly under `node`. Advisory (npm warns without engine-strict); an older Node fails with an opaque parse error before any runtime guard could fire.
//typescript: tsc (the last JS implementation — 6.x; 7.x is the Go port, whose npm package ships a binary with no in-process parser API) plays two roles here, both PARSE-only: the validity ORACLE for the tsc-corpus harvest (harvest_ts_repo.ts) and a parser ROW in the TS bench group (lib/tsc.ts). One definitional asymmetry to remember: tsc's parser is ERROR-RECOVERING — `createSourceFile` never throws, it returns a SourceFile plus `parseDiagnostics` — so an accept here means `parseDiagnostics.length === 0`, not `didn't throw`. Not one of the canonical-5 (nothing in the fixture corpus is baselined against it), so it bumps independently; keep it in the same MAJOR as the ../typescript checkout the corpus comes from, since a version below the corpus rejects the syntax the newer tests were written for.
//types: @types/node is types-only and dev-only (never ships, no runtime cost). It lets the shared harness's `node:` builtins type-check under `deno check` (and editors) when an npm package's .d.ts pulls in node types in npm-resolution mode — the portable-node:-builtins architecture's one new dev dep. NOT needed by the gated `deno task test:deno` (that's the dependency-free divergence suite — `node:assert` + relative imports, no node_modules).
//rsvelte-parse: @rsvelte/vite-plugin-svelte-native is a DIFFERENT package from @rsvelte/fmt below and versions independently of it: the N-API addon carrying rsvelte's compiler and, what earns it a place here, its PARSER. It backs two rows on parse/svelte — the only third-party engine on a surface whose other rows are svelte/compiler (the oracle) and tsv's own variants. Misleadingly named for a parse row, but it is the only in-process rsvelte parse surface with options: @rsvelte/compiler (also on npm) is a WASM lint/compile bundle whose parse_svelte takes no options and returns PRETTY-PRINTED JSON (the indentation happens inside the wasm before the string crosses the boundary, so there is no opting out), reports an internal version() rather than the upstream Svelte one, and drops Line comments this binding keeps. Rows: `rsvelte-parse` (mechanism- AND payload-matched to `tsv-json` — both compact JSON the caller parses, within ~1.5% on bytes) and `rsvelte-parse-skip-expr-loc`. ⚠ The latter is named for the OPTION, not for tsv's `no-locations` wire, because the reductions differ: tsv drops per-node `loc` throughout, skipExpressionLoc drops only nested expression loc and keeps top-level start/end. Two option paths give a row no reason to exist: skipCssAst is REJECTED by parse() (`only supported by parseEnvelope`), and the parseEnvelope path that honours it drops leadingComments relative to parse(), so it is lossier rather than a faster equal. It parses the whole conformance Svelte corpus with no host fault — re-check on a bump, since that is exactly where yuku's N-API binding segfaults. See lib/rsvelte_parse.ts.
//swc: @swc/core is the most widely deployed Rust TS/JS parser — parse-only here (swc ships no formatter), on BOTH the perf and conformance surfaces. Two properties decide how lib/swc.ts drives it. (1) Config must LAND: swc defaults `decorators: false` and accepts unknown option keys SILENTLY, so a decorated class fails with a bare 'Expression expected' that reads as a parser limit — init() parses a decorator to assert the option took effect. (2) It THROWS on invalid input, so an accept is an accept (no correction needed like yuku's error-tolerance or tsc's parseDiagnostics). Goal axis is spelled `isModule`, NOT `script` (the latter is inert — verified in both directions), which is what lets it score script-goal test262 files correctly. Its AST is its own dialect (root `Module`, `span` not `loc`, `Ts`-prefixed kinds), so it carries the oxc-class payload disclosure and is not an opponent for the span-only curated lines. Its real-corpus .d.ts rejections are catalogued in lib/perf_omit.ts — unlike oxc/yuku, swc rejects the ambient consts even with `dts: true` set explicitly, so those tolerances are the parser's own limit rather than a path-threading artifact.
//malva: dprint-plugin-malva is dprint's CSS formatter, loaded over the SAME @dprint/formatter host as @dprint/typescript — so it adds a wasm-tier engine to format/css for one more plugin wasm and no new machinery. The HTML plugin stays out (it does not format Svelte). The package ships ONLY *.wasm — no JS entry, hence no getPath() helper like @dprint/typescript has — so lib/malva.ts resolves the wasm file directly. CSS-only is enforced by the plugin itself ('unknown file extension' on .svelte/.ts, verified), and the unknown-key config diagnostic guard works the same as dprint's.
//postcss: postcss backs the first third-party engine on parse/css, earned on one argument: it is the parser behind prettier's CSS printer, i.e. behind the format/css BASELINE, which the parse surface therefore could not see. This is a standalone install, not the copy prettier vendors. No native peer can be added to that group: no Rust CSS parser exposes an AST to JS at all — lightningcss ships transform/bundle only (its ./ast export is types for the visitor callback, a napi round-trip per visited node), biome's js-api exposes formatContent/lintContent/openProject, malva is a formatter, and oxc's CSS is oxc_formatter_css with no JS parse binding. css-tree was evaluated for this slot and REJECTED: it parses an unclosed block without error even with onParseError supplied, so its accept rate would read ~100% vacuously; postcss throws there. Not payload-matched (a CSSOM-ish Root with nodes/raws, not the parseCss shape tsv is a drop-in for).
//rsvelte: @rsvelte/fmt is a CLI, not a library — the npm package is a Node launcher and the real formatter is a prebuilt binary carried by a platform `optionalDependency` (@rsvelte/fmt-<triple>), which is what lib/rsvelte.ts execs directly. Listing the launcher package is what pulls the right platform binary in; nothing imports it. Its only hard dep is prettier-plugin-tailwindcss (no transitive tree of its own), and its `oxfmt` peer is optional and unused here — .svelte formatting never leaves the binary. Because it has no in-process API its bench row is COVERAGE-ONLY (never timed) — see lib/rsvelte.ts and docs/benchmarks.md §Coverage-only rows.
//yuku: yuku-parser (N-API) and @yuku-parser/wasm are one Zig parser behind two bindings, versioned in lockstep — bump both together. Unlike the oxc wasi binding, the wasm package declares no `cpu`/`os`, so it installs as an ordinary dep on every host; the native package pulls its platform binary through `optionalDependencies` like oxc/oxfmt do. Both are PARSE-only (TS/JS — no Svelte, no CSS, no formatter), so they contribute rows to `parse/typescript` alone. Two properties of its JS API decide how lib/yuku.ts must drive it: `parse()` is LAZY (the AST materializes only when `.program` is read — a 1.69x/1.91x measured cost) and the parser is ERROR-TOLERANT (it never throws; an invalid file yields an empty AST plus `diagnostics`). One wrapper class drives both bindings, so both rows force `.program` and read `.diagnostics` by construction — see docs/benchmarks.md §Fairness caveats.
//oxc-wasi: The oxc-parser WASM bench row needs @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi — pure-wasm (runtime-portable) but its metadata declares `cpu: wasm32`, so npm skips it on any non-wasm host. It is NOT listed as a dep here: declaring it errors on x64, and as an optionalDependency npm records it as known-skipped so a later `--force` reinstall no-ops. Instead `deno task bench:install` (install_deps.ts) force-fetches it at the oxc-parser version (oxc ships all bindings in lockstep), so the `oxc-parser` pin above is its single source of truth too. ⚠ That lockstep is also a CEILING on the oxc-parser pin: from 0.143.0 the wasi binding fails to load under both Deno and Node with `this.bridge.setLastError is not a function` — it declares `@emnapi/core@2.0.0-alpha.3` and npm installs that NESTED, while the hoisted `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime` the binding also imports resolves its own `@emnapi/core` to the hoisted 1.x, so the two halves disagree. 0.142.0 is the newest version whose binding loads with no intervention, and an unloadable impl is ABSENT rather than fatal — init warns (`⚠ OXC WASM: not available`) but the COMMITTED report keeps no record, so the oxc-parser-wasm row just vanishes from both surfaces' tables. Re-probe on a bump (`import('@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi')`) before raising the pin; forcing `@emnapi/core`+`@emnapi/runtime` 2.0.0-alpha.3 to the tree root is a verified workaround, deliberately declined over hoisting an alpha to paper over an upstream mismatch.
